2222.title: Cursor provider: default model plus any MCP server with a non-string enum or tuple items yields an unactionable "Provider Error"

2222.proposedFix: (1) Picker policy in plugins/provider-acp/src/known-agents.ts: keep `auto` first but move `cursor-grok-4.6-medium` below the Claude/GPT/Composer families so the first alternative a user reaches for is a tolerant one; only demote `auto` once there is evidence it routes to Grok. (3) Optionally warn (not throw) at bb.agents.registerTool for non-string enum / tuple items next to the recursive-$ref guard, and stop stripping Cursor's "(NO ZDR)" marker so the privacy-mode failure is explainable from the picker.

2284.title: Workflows plugin: finished unstructured worker threads are never stopped, leaking idle provider processes
2284.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/workflows/src/service.ts handleThreadIdle settles unstructured (no outputSchema) calls and the structured freeform-JSON fallback as succeeded without calling stopChild(threadId), and no later run-level cleanup (settleRun/stop/recover only touch queued/running calls) or the daemon reaper (non-Codex excluded by default) ever releases the finished worker's per-thread provider process.

prReviews.topFinding: Does not address #2284 at all (only graduates the existing 30-min daemon reaper, useless for a burst that exhausts RAM in minutes); as a #1604 change it is 82 commits behind with content conflicts in runtime.ts/protocol.ts and bumps HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION 146->147 while main is at 164, and it deletes the only opt-out of forced 30-minute session release.

2284.proposedFix: In plugins/workflows/src/service.ts handleThreadIdle, add `await stopChild(threadId)` after `wakeCall(call)` in the unstructured `else` settle branch (return afterwards) and in the structured fallback-accepted branch (stored === accepted/idempotent). Verified: repro test goes 1/3 -> 3/3 and the full workflows suite (226 tests) stays green; diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/2284/repro/proposed-fix.diff. 2286.title: bb plugin list reports `handlers: 0 errors` while a plugin throws on every call
2286.rootCauseOneLine: handlerStats.errorCount is incremented only inside invokeWrapped (request-shaped surfaces: http/rpc/cli/tools/events/mentions/schedules); background-service crashes and uncaught exceptions go through onServiceSettled/handleUncaughtException which only logger.warn and restart with backoff (status stays running, nothing counted), and bb.log.error from a plugin that catches its own exception is never aggregated at all.

In plugin-api.ts emitLog, count level === "error" calls (either into errorCount or a new additive handlerStats.loggedErrorCount in packages/server-contract) and set statusDetail to the latest message. Change apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts printPlugin to print the handlers line when count > 0 || errorCount > 0. Optionally surface a time-windowed "Failing" signal in the desktop plugin UI, which today deliberately never renders handlerStats. No server/daemon wire change, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. The three failing tests in the repro file become the regression tests.

2289.title: Pi provider: stale model catalog after models.json change; plugin reload never retires superseded bridge workers
2289.rootCauseOneLine: pi's RPC get_available_models returns a boot-time snapshot (models.json is only re-read in ModelRuntime.refresh(), which bb never triggers), the pi bridge memoizes one long-lived `pi --mode rpc --no-session` catalog child per cwd, the daemon keeps that bridge worker across plugin reloads because its process key (artifact digest + declaration fingerprint) never changes, and the server additionally memoizes provider.list_models for 10 minutes keyed by registration revision.
2289.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-pi/src/bridge/catalog.ts, fingerprint pi's models.json (resolve the agent dir as pi does: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR else ~/.pi/agent; hash content or mtimeMs+size) when the catalog child is spawned, compare on every fetchRaw()/probe(), and on change kill the child so spawnChild() respawns it (it already handles child.exited); this fixes the data staleness at the plugin layer without touching the daemon process key. Separately, shorten or fingerprint-key the server's 10-minute providerModelList memo (apps/server/src/lifecycle-dedupers.ts) or document `bb plugin reload provider-pi` as the refresh path, since it already bumps the memo key. The included vitest (real pinned pi, isolated agent dir) fails on base and should pass with the change.
2289.caveats: The "repeated reloads leak duplicate bridge workers" claim does not reproduce at 494f66526: three reloads left exactly one provider-pi worker under the dev daemon; extra workers are per-environment thread runtime processes (by design) or other dev daemons on this machine. The reporter's 0.39.0 build predates the 60 s provider-maintenance-runtime idle shutdown (d74974183/#1879) and the server memo (189be3eb3/#1885), so on 0.39.0 the stale worker really did live until killed by hand; at base the worker is recycled after 60 s without maintenance requests, but the server memo still hides changes for up to 10 minutes and any request within 60 s keeps the stale worker warm. GitHub project fields (Type/Effort) could not be read with the available token scopes. Reproduced against pi 0.84.2 on PATH and the pinned 0.84.0; no screenshots since the bug is not visual (the app picker reads the same memoized execution-options endpoint as the CLI). The repro test file remains in the worktree at plugins/provider-pi/src/bridge/catalog.models-json-staleness.test.ts; its vitest scratch dir is removed by the test's afterAll.

2298.title: Archiving a thread leaves its native browser views alive
2298.rootCauseOneLine: Since ce006c6ea browser WebContentsViews are retained on unmount and destroyed only on tab close / thread delete / environment delete; neither the UI archive action (ThreadActionsProvider.archiveThreadAndChildrenAction) nor the archived-changed broadcast handler calls destroyPersistedBrowserViewsForThread, and the main process never reclaims views except on window close, so each archived thread's preview renderer stays alive (hidden, not animating) until the window closes.
2298.proposedFix: Mirror delete's teardown at both archive entry points (validated again in worktree wf_846839f8-f8a-17, diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/2298/repro/proposed-fix.diff): (1) in apps/app/src/components/thread/ThreadActionsProvider.tsx archiveThreadAndChildrenAction, after closePanesForThreads(response.archivedThreadIds), call destroyPersistedBrowserViewsForThread({desktopBrowser: getDesktopBrowserApi(), threadId}) for every archived id; (2) in apps/app/src/hooks/cache-owners/resource-route-owner.ts handle thread messages whose changes include "archived-changed" the same way as "thread-deleted" (covers bb thread archive / SDK / automations / other windows; no-op on unarchive). Keep thread_tabs untouched so unarchive recreates the page lazily. With the fix: repro test 2/2 pass, 57 files / 385 neighbouring tests pass, turbo typecheck @bb/app --force passes, and live (fix-validation.sh) the sidebar archive removes the CDP target and renderer pid 1801 while thread_tabs still holds the browser tab; unarchive + reopen creates a fresh target (30EA1588) and the page reloads. Open design point: a wire archive while the thread is viewed destroys the view under a mounted tab (blank until reselected); alternative is to defer teardown to deck unmount when thread.archivedAt is set. Follow-ups (not this issue): the renderer-side view registry is lost on any app-window reload, orphaning native views (reproduced again as samples row 5), so ownership should move to the main process; and no age/pressure policy exists for views hidden via Cmd+J.

2299.title: Builtin memory/automations/custom-instructions CLIs silently ignore unknown flags (core bb and tasks reject them)
2299.rootCauseOneLine: bb forwards plugin argv untouched ("parsing argv is plugin-owned") and the memory, automations, custom-instructions, and provider-retry plugins each hand-roll a parser that collects every --x into a map and only reads known names, with no leftover check like tasks' assertAllowed(), so unknown flags (e.g. --details-file) are silently dropped and the verb still writes and exits 0.

Structurally, ship a shared strict argv helper (tasks/cli/args.ts shape: parseArgs + assertAllowed + option/requireOption) in @get-bb/plugin-sdk under an experimental_ name with a docs/api_to_audit.md entry, and migrate the builtin plugins onto it. No wire changes, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. Risk: scripts passing stale/misspelled flags start failing, which is the intent.

2308.title: Idle provider bridge processes are never retired for non-Codex providers
2308.rootCauseOneLine: releaseIdleProviderProcess only calls retireSupersededBridgeProcessIfIdle, which no-ops for a current-artifact bridge, and no idle timer or sweep ever revisits a zero-thread environment bridge (evictIdleEnvironments has no production caller; the 30-min session reaper only reaches stopThread, which lands in the same no-op, and for non-Codex providers only runs at all when the providerSessionReaping experiment is on), so one bridge per (environment, provider) stays resident until daemon exit; since e42a4ef48 (#2325) removed the Codex thread-scoped exemption this applies to Codex too.
2308.proposedFix: Do not adopt the issue's patch (unconditional shutdown at threadIds.size === 0): on base it breaks 8 existing tests (re-confirmed this run: 8 failed / 101 passed, identical list) that encode deliberate warm-process reuse, including the #1604 reaper's resume-on-same-process contract. Instead add a bounded idle retirement: track idleSinceMs on RuntimeProviderProcess (set at spawn and when threadIds becomes empty, cleared when a thread attaches); add RuntimeProviderProcessManager.retireIdleProviderProcesses({ idleForMs, nowMs }) that shutdownProvider()s processes with zero threads, idle past the threshold, not in providerStarting and with no pending requests; expose it on AgentRuntime and call it from the existing 5-minute daemon sweep (runtime.reapIdleProviderSessions / RuntimeManager.reapIdleProviderSessions) with a bridge threshold of ~5 min (matches plugin-host workers), and make it independent of the providerSessionReaping experiment (which gates the session reaper for non-Codex providers and defaults to false). Keep retireSupersededBridgeProcessIfIdle for the immediate superseded-artifact case. No wire shape changes, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump unless the threshold becomes a server policy field. Tests: the repro test adapted to invoke the sweep (fails before/passes after), a below-threshold or thread-attached bridge survives, and a sweep during ensureProvider startup does not kill the starting process.
2308.caveats: Revision addressed all verifier findings: the '#1604 reaper enabled' claim is now 'Partially verified' with the providerSessionReaping gating (experiments.ts:34 default false; runtime.ts:1008-1018; session.ts:43; app.ts:700-704) spelled out in the claims table, step 7 and section 5; bridges.sh prints exe + last 100 chars of the command so bridge vs plugin-host processes are identifiable, and all live artifacts were re-captured on a fresh instance (ports 14861/22861/30861, worktree wf_846839f8-f8a-21, daemon pid 17027, bridge pid 20879 resident with 0 children across two stop cycles, 9.5 min total, plus a 10-s watch log); bbdev.sh now derives ports from scripts/bb-dev-app env (plus setup-project.sh / wait-idle.sh); the per-environment keying citation now points at runtime-manager.ts:1033 and :366-368. Remaining caveats unchanged: issue was filed against 8bd6acc9 and base 494f66526 (== origin/main, re-fetched this run) already contains #2325, so the title's 'non-Codex' qualifier is stale; the reporter's ~78 MB/960 MB figures are unverified (my tsx-run idle bridge was 96-256 MB RSS); GitHub project fields were not readable; no screenshots (no UI surface). 2316.title: Side-chat reply anchor is persisted but omitted from the first provider turn
2316.rootCauseOneLine: A seed-only idle fork persists the agent-only reply seed in its thread-start client/turn/requested event but hands the daemon providerInput [] (intentional no-input-no-turn), and neither the direct first send nor the queued auto-send (both via prepareTurnSubmitCommandPayload) ever reads that persisted seed back, so the model never receives it.
2316.proposedFix: In apps/server/src/services/threads/thread-commands.ts prepareTurnSubmitCommandPayload (the choke point for both the direct first send and the queued-message auto-send), when target.mode === "start" and input is non-empty, look up the thread's own agent-initiated thread-start client/turn/requested row; if all its inputs are visibility "agent-only" and no turn/started event exists after it, prepend those inputs to input (and to inputGroups[0]). Prototype diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/2316/repro/proposed-fix.diff: repro test passes, apps/server test/threads + test/public pass (57 files / 597 tests), @bb/server typecheck passes, and live on a patched server the Codex wire shows the seed ahead of the user's question, the model answers with the anchored message, and the seed is not repeated on the second turn. A real PR should add a 'second turn does not repeat the seed' test and apply the same helper to the non-fork seed-without-run lazy thread.start path (fork === null, non-empty input only). No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed (wire shape unchanged).
2316.caveats: The user-visible wrong answer (BANANA instead of APPLE) is model behaviour and was demonstrated once per fork, not statistically; the definitive evidence is the failing server test and the bridge wire recordings. For point forks (replying to an assistant message that has a completed turn) the seed is equally dropped but the cloned session already ends at that message, so the model often guesses right; the tip-fork fallback (replying to the opening user message or a selection) is where users notice. Side observation: the hidden fork's fallback title is derived from the agent-only seed text and leaks it when the fork is opened as a full thread. The worktree retains the prototype fix and the new test file (uncommitted) for review. Duplicate search was a spot check, not exhaustive.

2323.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/automations/src/cli.ts parseArgs only treats --help/-h as help when it is argv[0]; elsewhere --help becomes an unread boolean flag and -h a positional, and the core bb CLI forwards plugin argv raw to the server so commander's help/unknown-option handling never runs, so update/pause/resume/run/delete/create execute their service call.

2327.title: turn/completed can precede command completion and wedge later turns between active-writer and no-session errors
2327.rootCauseOneLine: Codex >= 0.146 holds a per-process flock writer lock on each loaded thread; bb's codex bridge reopens rollouts via thread/resume in a fresh app-server (after release, settings/auth rebuild, bridge restart, env move) without waiting for its previous child to exit or recognising a foreign writer, and treats Codex's "already has an active writer" refusal as an untyped bridge error (recovery: null) so the turn is rejected, the thread goes to error, stop/retry resumes the same locked rollout, and (pre-#2325) the bridge forgot the thread while the runtime kept it, yielding "No active codex session" on the next turn.
2327.proposedFix: (1) In the codex bridge's constructThreadSession and thread/stop{release}, await the old app-server connection's finalized exit before spawning/resuming the replacement so bb never races its own previous writer. (2) Classify Codex's "thread <id> already has an active writer" (regex next to CODEX_ARCHIVED_SESSION_ERROR_PATTERN) into a typed retryable recovery hint (e.g. sessionBusy); have the runtime's actOnRejection retry the construction with bounded backoff and otherwise raise a typed error so the server records a specific system/error ("Codex thread is open in another program") and keeps the thread idle with the input queued instead of flipping to error; bump HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION and document the hint. (3) After a turn/start rejected by a construction failure, forget the thread in the runtime exactly as a rejected thread/resume does so the next send always goes through resume and "No active codex session" cannot appear for this cause. (4) Add fake-app-server scripted "active writer" refusals and bridge tests for rebuild-waits-for-old-child, typed hint + retry, and release->resume; keep the real-Codex vitest as opt-in.
2327.caveats: Revise pass: the verifier's major finding (4a did not run as written) was fixed by making codex-writer-lock.mjs create its cwd and CODEX_HOME, refuse ~/.codex, and warn when auth.json is missing; the step now lists the mkdir + cp auth.json prerequisite and was re-run from scratch at 494f66526 (codex-writer-lock.log overwritten in place). 4b was re-run on a fresh dev instance (ports 17285/25285/33285, thread thr_dyn6jcqggc -> codex 01a034dc-fdc9-...) with the placeholder-free commands now in the report (scratch git repo step, DATA_DIR derived from `scripts/bb-dev-app status`, host id from `pnpm bb:dev machine list`); all outputs, the event dump, the daemon log excerpt and the "recovered" screenshot were replaced from that run (event sequence 19-43 identical to the first run; the "before" and "error" screenshots are from the first run and show the same states). 4c was re-run with the explicit cp-into-package step and BB_2327_SLOW_WRAPPER; 2 passed. The TL;DR, claims table and section 5.3 now state that "No active codex session" is verified at the bridge level only: the base-commit runtime forgets the thread after a refused resume (abandonFailedSessionConstruction, runtime.ts#L2107-L2116), so end to end at 494f66526 every retry reports "already has an active writer" and the exact pair from the issue is reachable only with the pre-#2325 bridge (code trace; the old bridge.ts cannot run against the current SDK). The issue's "turn/completed before item/completed" claim remains unverified Codex-side ordering not needed for the wedge. Scenario B uses a wrapper that delays SIGTERM by 1.5 s; on Codex 0.149.1 the natural self-race window is ~10 ms, so foreign writers are the realistic trigger. The issue gives no bb/Codex versions. origin/main up to 21cb6b68b has no fix (later commits in the relevant packages are test-only). 2328.title: Automatic recovery storms a dead Codex thread with repeated no-active-session errors
2328.rootCauseOneLine: Host-daemon split-brain: the agent-runtime keeps the thread registered (so resumeThreadRuntimeIfMissing never resumes) while the codex bridge has released the session (so every turn/start is rejected with untyped -32000 "No active codex session"); proven trigger is the 30s runtime JSON-RPC timeout on thread/stop vs the bridge's 60s+5s interrupt budget, and each rejected send re-emits thread.failed, which re-arms the reporter's external bb-collab recovery loop.
2328.proposedFix: (1) Add a typed SESSION_NOT_FOUND code to BRIDGE_JSON_RPC_ERRORS, return it from the codex bridge's requireLiveSessionForTurn/handleTurnSteer (and pi/ACP equivalents), and in runtime.runTurn/steerTurn forget the thread registration on that code so the daemon's next turn.submit resumes the session from its rollout. (2) In runtime.stopThread, distinguish a bridge rejection (JsonRpcResponseError: keep state) from no answer (timeout/process exit: forget the thread), and give thread/stop a request timeout that covers the bridge's interrupt budget (>=65s for codex); validated variant in candidate-fix-runtime-stop-timeout.diff makes the desired-invariant test pass with 115/115 existing runtime tests green. (3) Server policy: do not emit a fresh thread.failed for a turn.submit rejected before any provider turn when the thread is already in error with the same detail (or include dedup context), fix the composer's "Retry by sending a follow-up message" hint for this state, and surface stop failures instead of returning {ok:true} after a 30s daemon timeout.

2225.title: Claude Code api_retry events remain unclassifiable when the SDK reports unknown/null status; turns can stall through blind retry storms
2225.rootCauseOneLine: The Claude Code CLI's api_retry classifier (aen(e) in the binary) only inspects e.status, so connection-level failures are emitted as error "unknown"/error_status null and bb can only relay category "unknown"; bb additionally has no per-turn retry guardrail (only the runtime's idle tracking reads willRetry), drops classification on the terminal error, and — a separate bb bug not in the issue — its claudeAssistantMessageErrorSchema lacks the SDK's "overloaded" value so HTTP 529 retries are downgraded to thread-scoped provider/unhandled rows instead of provider/error.

(3) Server/runtime-owned guardrail: count consecutive willRetry:true provider/error per turn (reset on progress) and past a conservative threshold interrupt via the existing stop path with a terminal provider/error (willRetry:false, last errorInfo) or emit a distinct "upstream unreachable" event; cheaper alternative is launching the CLI with a lower CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES. 2318.rootCauseOneLine: The command-mention pill serializes as bare `/name` with no word-boundary guard (prompt-editor-serialization.ts#L980-L996) — the pick-time space is the only separator, it is trimmed on send (prompt-draft.ts#L268-L270) and every restore path (history recall, queued/sent-message edit) and insertTextAtCursor put text directly behind the pill; independently the claude-code bridge forwards the text verbatim (bridge.ts buildPromptText) and Claude Code 2.1.197 only expands `/skill` when it is the first token of the prompt, so a mid-message chip is never run as a skill.

The two failing tests in 2318/repro/issue-2318-skill-chip.test.tsx become the regression tests. (2) Claude Code skill invocation: hoist a `source: "skill"` command mention to the head of the prompt (`/name <rest>`) so Claude Code's start-of-prompt slash parser expands it — ideally in the claude-code bridge's buildPromptText (requires promptInputItemSchema to keep `mentions`, bridge.ts#L132-L136; bump HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION if the daemon does not already forward input items verbatim), or at the server send boundary next to resolvePromptMode which already interprets the /plan pill by mention metadata regardless of position. Guard: multiple skill chips, chips inside code spans, and keep the timeline's displayed user text unchanged.

2322.title: env.json writers can silently overwrite concurrent updates
2322.rootCauseOneLine: bb-app env set/unset (and config set/unset) do an unsynchronized read-snapshot -> patch -> temp-file rename of env.json in packages/bb-app/src/launcher.ts (L1254-L1283, L1999-L2013), so two concurrent writers both start from the same stale snapshot and the last rename silently discards the other writer's change (16/20 lost updates at process level, deterministic in-process).
2322.proposedFix: Add one launcher helper mutateManagedJsonFile({dataDir, fileName, mutate}) that takes an exclusive lock file (<dataDir>/.<file>.lock via open(...,'wx',0o600) with bounded retry and stale-lock age check), then reads the current document, applies the mutation, writes the 0o600 temp file and renames it, releasing the lock in finally. Route env set, env unset, config set, config unset and the client.json writer through it (deleting the separate read-then-write sequences in runEnvCommand/runConfigCommand), keep input validation before the lock, and turn the two in-process repro cases plus a spawn-based two-process case into regression tests. No file-format, server, daemon, or protocol change is needed (no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump).
2322.caveats: The issue's 'authorized plugin' writer does not exist: no plugin API, server route, desktop, CLI, or host-daemon code writes env.json; the server only reads it on reload. The realistic race is two bb-app env/config processes at once. Issue line numbers (1183-1211, 1905-1938) are stale against base 494f66526 (actual 1169-1184/1254-1283 and 1979-2032). The same defect affects config.json (8/10 lost updates) and client.json. The first vitest run accidentally sent the harmless post-write reload POST to the orchestration shell's BB_SERVER_URL (127.0.0.1:62937, not the user's :38886) because the launcher prefers that env var over --server-port; the logged runs were redone with it unset and the scripts/test now guard for it. No screenshots (non-visual bug). pnpm dev:stop reported stopping one leftover pid (34963) during cleanup; no dev instance was ever started, no dev data dir existed, and all ports/scratch dirs were confirmed clean.

2326.title: Visible unarchived threads are absent from the app list until opened by direct link
2326.rootCauseOneLine: The sidebar buckets threads by their root ancestor's project (createSidebarProjectIdResolver, introduced by PR #1849) and only renders children while the parent row is expanded (collapse state persisted in localStorage), so a lane spawned in project P by a director in another project (or under a collapsed parent) never appears in P's group, while the server/CLI group by thread.projectId; opening the thread by direct link runs the ProjectList effect that expands all collapsed ancestors, which is why it then "appears".
2326.proposedFix: In apps/app/src/components/sidebar/ProjectList.tsx `threadsByProject`, bucket by `thread.projectId` instead of `createSidebarProjectIdResolver` so a cross-project child renders as a root in its own project group (buildThreadTreeItems already treats a thread whose parent is outside the bucket as a root); reuse the existing ThreadRow `crossProjectId` marker in the reverse direction ("child of <parent> in <project>") and keep the resolver only for the selected-thread expansion effect (expanding the thread's own project group). Separately, make hidden children explicit: when a collapsed parent gains a new child (thread-created with parentThreadId in collapsedThreadIds) auto-expand it or show a "+N" badge from node.stats.childCount. Add the client-core regression test (for every visible unarchived thread t, the group built for t.projectId contains t) and an app-level ProjectList test that a child of a collapsed parent remains discoverable after a thread-created realtime message. Risk: reverses #1849's UX decision to nest cross-project children under the parent; do not render a thread in both groups because windowed-list keys and keyboard navigation are keyed by thread id.
2326.caveats: The reporter did not include parentThreadId (or the parent's project) for thr_8n32y4ujbs / thr_s5843imarf, so the mapping of this mechanism onto their exact data is inferred from the "tenant lane / director" wording; confirming requires `bb thread show <id> --json | jq .parentThreadId` and the parent's projectId plus the operator's sidebar collapse state. All alternative causes the issue suggested (bootstrap filtering, realtime invalidation, hidden->visible flips, hidden-tab deferral, offline/reconnect catch-up, the 30-thread placeholder cap, windowing, machine grouping) were exercised live and behaved correctly; E4 used Chrome offline emulation which kept the socket open (queued frames), so a true dead-socket reconnect was only code-reviewed, not live-tested. Threads were created with the pi provider, which fails instantly on this machine (expired OAuth); list membership does not depend on status so this does not affect the repro. The worktree contains the added test file packages/client-core/test/sidebarProjectMembership.repro-2326.test.ts (also copied to the report dir); origin/main (21cb6b68b) has no changes to the sidebar grouping code.

2334.title: Legacy @bb/plugin-sdk alias not registered in source dev mode (pnpm dev / dev:desktop), breaking plugins on the pre-rename specifier
2334.rootCauseOneLine: plugin-runtime.ts builds the jiti alias map (both @get-bb/plugin-sdk and legacy @bb/plugin-sdk) only when dist/plugin-sdk-runtime.js exists next to the running module; under tsx (pnpm dev, vitest) import.meta.url is src/services/plugins/, the file never exists there, so the alias is silently undefined and the legacy specifier has no resolution path (the current name still resolves via jiti's createRequire fallback from apps/server/node_modules).

prReviews.topFinding: Aliasing both SDK specifiers to the resolved src/index.ts is a jiti prefix rewrite, so every SDK subpath import becomes …/src/index.ts/<sub>; on current main (post-#2325) this makes all four first-party provider plugins (codex, claude-code, pi, acp) fail to load under pnpm dev with Cannot find module '…/packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts/host'. Verified live and with a loader-level test that passes on 494f66526 and fails with the PR cherry-picked. The PR branch is based on 836e216c7 (pre-#2325), which is why the author's manual verification passed; GitHub still reports it MERGEABLE.

2334.proposedFix: In apps/server/src/services/plugins/plugin-runtime.ts, when dist/plugin-sdk-runtime.js is absent (source mode), do not alias @get-bb/plugin-sdk at all (it and its subpaths resolve naturally via jiti's createRequire fallback) and alias only the legacy @bb/plugin-sdk name, one alias key per SDK export subpath (., ./host, ./ai-services, ./provider-bridge, ./provider-bridge/acp, ./provider-bridge/testing, ./app, ./internal/*), each mapped to fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve("@get-bb/plugin-sdk" + subpath)); jiti matches longest key first, verified in the jiti-alias-experiment. Add loader-level regression tests (legacy-sdk-alias-source-mode.test.ts: 3 cases; sdk-subpath-source-mode.test.ts: subpath import from a source plugin). Deeper follow-up: packaged servers have the mirror problem (only plugin-sdk-runtime.js is shipped, so a source-loaded plugin importing a subpath resolves to plugin-sdk-runtime.js/host); emit one runtime bundle per SDK export and build the same per-subpath alias map from them.
2334.caveats: Did not run a packaged/nightly build to confirm the legacy alias works there (consistent with code: packages/bb-app/server/dist/plugin-sdk-runtime.js exists next to the server bundle). The issue's claim that only the source-fallback branch is affected is partly wrong: a prebuilt dist/server.js that imports @bb/plugin-sdk fails identically in source mode (third test case). The Extensions detail-page copy differs slightly for a path install vs the npm install quoted in the issue. The proposed per-export alias fix was validated only at the jiti resolution level, not as a full implementation. Two repro test files were left untracked in the worktree (apps/server/test/services/plugins/legacy-sdk-alias-source-mode.test.ts and sdk-subpath-source-mode.test.ts); local branches repro-2334 (at 494f66526) and pr2335-on-base (PR cherry-picked) exist in the worktree; nothing was pushed or commented.

2224.title: Claude Code provider: sdk/system background_tasks_changed falls into assertNever and surfaces as provider/unhandled debug rows
2224.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/provider-claude-code/src/visibility.ts keeps a closed allow-list of sdk/system subtypes; the newer Claude CLI (2.1.241, newer than the 2.1.197 bundled with the pinned SDK 0.3.197) emits background_tasks_changed on every background-task start/settle, which the list collapses to coverage "unknown", so delta-translation's unhandledDeltas() emits an `unhandled` delta and the runtime persists a provider/unhandled row (two per task); nothing throws — the assertNever branch the issue blames is unreachable.
2224.proposedFix: Add "background_tasks_changed" to visibility.ts in three places: the ClaudeSystemSubtype union, the toClaudeSystemSubtype() switch, and the noise case group in describeParsedClaudeRawEvent (the task_started/task_updated/task_notification bookends already drive bb's backgroundTask items, so the CLI's level signal carries nothing bb needs). Verified: the 2-test repro passes, the existing visibility/delta-translation/task-translation suites (80 tests) pass, and the plugin typecheck passes with the 7-line diff in /tmp/bb-reports/issues/2224/repro/proposed-fix.diff. No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump is needed (no server/daemon wire shape changes). Recommended in the same PR: also classify the other subtypes CLI 2.1.241 already emits that bb does not list (feedback_draft_queued, task_summary, post_turn_summary, control_request_progress, code_change_published, vcs_state_changed, worker_shutting_down, informational) as noise, and keep the raw subtype in the "unknown" description's kind so future unhandled rows name what they are instead of the bare "sdk/system".
2224.caveats: The issue's mechanism claim is wrong: toClaudeSystemSubtype maps unlisted subtypes to "unknown" and the "unknown" case is handled, so assertNever never throws; the symptom (provider/unhandled rows) comes from the coverage-"unknown" path. Reproduced live against the user's PATH claude 2.1.241 (the plugin prefers PATH over the SDK-bundled 2.1.197, which does not emit this subtype), so installs running an older CLI will not see the rows. The "Unhandled Claude Code event" UI row is visible by default only in dev builds; packaged builds persist the event but render it only when the "Show unhandled provider events" setting is on. The additional unlisted subtypes were found by string-extracting the CLI binary, not observed on the wire.

2288.title: Cmd+click on a thread link should open the macOS default browser instead of the in-app browser
2288.rootCauseOneLine: MarkdownAnchor.handleAnchorClick in apps/app/src/components/ui/markdown-preview.tsx routes every http(s) link through linkRouting.onOpenLink (in-app browser) and calls preventDefault() without checking metaKey/ctrlKey/shiftKey/altKey, unlike useUrlAnchorClickHandler, RouteAnchor and PluginUrlLink which all bail on modified clicks, so Cmd+click never falls through to the anchor's target=_blank default that Electron's setWindowOpenHandler would hand to shell.openExternal.
2288.proposedFix: In MarkdownAnchor.handleAnchorClick (apps/app/src/components/ui/markdown-preview.tsx), after the local-file and app-route branches and before consulting linkRouting.onOpenLink, return early when event.defaultPrevented || event.button !== 0 || event.altKey || event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey || event.shiftKey. Falling through is sufficient: the anchor has target="_blank", so on desktop the main window's setWindowOpenHandler already calls shell.openExternal and denies the popup, and on web the browser opens its own tab. Verified: the repro test goes 3 failed -> 5 passed, typecheck clean, and live in the Electron shell Cmd+click no longer creates an in-app browser target while a plain click still does. Preferably extract a shared isPlainPrimaryClick(event) helper and use it from useUrlAnchorClickHandler, RouteAnchor, PluginUrlLink, ExperimentalFileLink and MarkdownAnchor so the predicate cannot drift again. No protocol/IPC change, no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
2288.caveats: Live repro drove the Electron dev shell via CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent with the Meta modifier bit rather than a physical trackpad Cmd+click; the in-app browser opening was observed via the CDP target list plus DOM probe and screenshots (the browser WebContentsView body is blank in host-page screenshots). After the fixed Cmd+click I could not directly confirm the OS browser received the URL: Safari was running but reading its tab URL requires an Automation permission prompt, so that half is inferred from the existing setWindowOpenHandler path. Page.windowOpen CDP events never fire in Electron when setWindowOpenHandler denies, so they are not usable evidence. Issue has no Type/Effort set on GitHub; priority Low came from the task prompt. Worktree left with only the new repro test file (fix reverted); dev instance, data dir, launcher logs and scratch repo were removed and ports 16135/24135/32135/45288 confirmed free.

2290.title: compactThread returns 409 for acp-omp although the provider-acp bridge already implements /compact
2290.rootCauseOneLine: The acp-omp entry in plugins/provider-acp/src/known-agents.ts omits supportsManualCompaction (opencode sets it), so the server's compactThreadContext gate 409s and the composer hides /compact before the bridge's working /compact maintenance-prompt path is ever reached; additionally, omp answers end_turn even when its /compact fails ("Nothing to compact"), so lifting the gate alone yields a false thread/compacted.

prReviews.topFinding: Unmergeable: it patches ACP_PROVIDERS in plugins/provider-acp/server.ts, which #2325 (e42a4ef48) removed; the property must move to the acp-omp entry in plugins/provider-acp/src/known-agents.ts. Also, un-gating exposes a false thread/compacted + 'Context compacted' banner when omp replies 'Compaction failed: Nothing to compact (session too small)' with end_turn (reproduced live twice), contradicting the PR's 'fails the turn legibly' claim; mirror the pi plugin's compaction-skipped handling (#1721) or scope it out explicitly.

2290.proposedFix: (1) Add `supportsManualCompaction: true` to the `acp-omp` entry in plugins/provider-acp/src/known-agents.ts (verified: PR tests + repro pass, typecheck green, live POST returns 200; no protocol bump needed since the flag is server-internal); update the first-party capability table test and add the acp-omp 200-path case to public-thread-compaction.test.ts. (2) In packages/provider-bridge-acp startCompaction, detect omp's agent message 'Compaction failed: …' during the compaction prompt and finish with status failed — or treat 'Nothing to compact (session too small)' / 'Already compacted' as a skipped compaction (provider.warning category compaction-skipped, completed boundary, no context.compacted), exactly as plugins/provider-pi/src/delta-translation.ts does; cover with a fake-ACP-agent bridge test.
2290.caveats: Live repro used omp 16.3.10 (issue cites OMP 17.4.1 nightly) on a 2-message session, so the successful-compaction path was not observed live; only the small-session false-positive was. The issue comment's production success on a 73k-token thread is unverifiable from here. The second `thread tell` in step 06 did not append a provider turn, so both compaction attempts hit the same small session. The 'fixed' screenshots were captured via the dev server's plugin hot-reload of my one-line change, and the 'base' screenshots after reverting it (07-recapture-base.sh confirms 409 and empty command list before capture). Worktree left on branch pr-2293-ported with the ported PR commit plus a staged revert of known-agents.ts and the untracked repro test.

2291.title: provider.list_models startup probe logs "ACP agent is not authenticated." at warn on every daemon start
2291.rootCauseOneLine: CommandRouter.handleOnlineRpcRequest warns "online host RPC failed" for every online-RPC failure whose code is not in EXPECTED_ONLINE_RPC_FAILURE_CODES ({file_too_large, provision_cancelled}); the typed AgentRuntimeRecoveryError{code:"auth_required"} from the ACP model-list probe is therefore logged at warn in the daemon even though the same code is returned to the server, which logs and surfaces it itself. The issue's "startup race with the ACP auth handshake" is refuted: the probe just execFiles `cursor-agent --list-models`, which on this machine fails persistently ("Logged in" but "Authentication required"), so the warn fires on every execution-options read, not once per daemon start.

prReviews.topFinding: The one-line source change (add "auth_required" to EXPECTED_ONLINE_RPC_FAILURE_CODES) is correct and does silence the warn on main (verified with a router-level test), but the PR's regression test is dead on arrival: it passes bare `new Error("ACP agent is not authenticated.")` objects and relies on the daemon's ACP_AUTH_REQUIRED_PATTERN message regex, which e42a4ef48 (#2325) deleted from main after the PR was opened; cherry-picked onto 494f66526 the test file conflicts (git merge-tree CONFLICT) and, once resolved, the new test fails (`expected false to be true` at command-dispatch-support.test.ts:21). Needs a rebase, a test that throws a typed AgentRuntimeRecoveryError through CommandRouter, a note that the allow-list applies to every online RPC type (provider.usage/installation.*, plugin.host.call), and removal of the unfounded "auth handshake race" wording.

2291.proposedFix: In apps/host-daemon/src/command-dispatch-support.ts either add "auth_required" (and "rate_limited", the only other AgentRuntimeRecoveryError code) to EXPECTED_ONLINE_RPC_FAILURE_CODES, or — narrower — make isExpectedOnlineRpcFailureError return true for `error instanceof AgentRuntimeRecoveryError` (typed recovery rejections are provider/user state by construction, never daemon bugs). Keep the debug "Online host RPC" accounting line and the typed errorCode in the response untouched; leave the server's "Failed to resolve provider models" warn and the auth_required empty-fallback policy alone. Regression test: the router-level test in the report (throws a typed auth_required error via listModels, asserts ok:false/errorCode:auth_required, debug line fired, zero warn calls) — fails on 494f66526, passes with either fix. No wire change, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
2291.caveats: The reporter's "one warn per daemon session, later probes succeed" observation could not be verified: on this machine cursor-agent --list-models is rejected persistently (stale Cursor credential: status says Logged in but cannot fetch user details), so every execution-options read warns; there is nothing in the code that makes the warn startup-only. The issue/PR's claims about a message-regex classifier (getErrorCode L149-150) and a sibling test were true at fff3ae8 but are gone at base after e42a4ef48. The issue's claim that the picker falls back to declared models on auth_required is wrong at base (listFallbackModelsForLoadError returns [] for auth_required; live response models=[]). No screenshots: this is a log-noise bug, evidence is the API responses and log lines. PR #2294 had no CI checks recorded at review time (GitHub API briefly rate-limited during the investigation).

2292.title: prompt history: empty-array rows persisted then skipped at read (zod too_small; 11 rows observed)
2292.rootCauseOneLine: recordAcceptedPromptHistoryEntry persists args.input unconditionally; a no-prompt fork (bb thread fork without --prompt, SDK threads.fork without input, unseeded side-chat launcher fork) is user-initiated and root-level (forks are not hierarchy children, parentThreadId null) so it resolves to project scope and writes input "[]", which the read schema z.array(...).min(1) rejects and drops with a warn on every read.

prReviews.topFinding: Fixes the root cause at the single write funnel with a test that fails on base (verified: PR test fails at prompt-history.test.ts:512 'expected true to be false' without the guard); applies cleanly to 494f66526, typecheck green, 9/9 tests pass, and a live no-prompt fork on a patched dev instance wrote no row. Only gap (low): no one-off cleanup of already-persisted input='[]' rows, so affected users keep getting the warn on every history read until they are deleted. CI has not run (cross-repo PR, needs workflow approval).

2292.proposedFix: Guard the single write funnel (apps/server/src/services/prompt-history.ts recordAcceptedPromptHistoryEntry): return false without inserting when args.input.length === 0, exactly as PR #2295 does; keep the read-side skip as defense in depth. Optionally add a Drizzle migration DELETE FROM prompt_history_entries WHERE input = '[]' to stop perpetual warns for users who already have bad rows. No wire change, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump; callers ignore the return value and new-turn targets already require min(1) input at the API boundary.
2292.caveats: The issue's "11 rows in production" and acp-omp provider claims are unverifiable (private DB); mechanism confirmed with codex instead. The side-chat UI path was not driven in a browser; only unseeded side-chat forks (launcher tip fork, or anchor equal to the last message) reach the user-initiated write, seeded ones start as agent and never write a row. No screenshots because the bug has no visual surface (the app hides empty drafts). Adjacent unfiled observation: forks carrying both agentContextSeed and a visible prompt store the agent-only seed item in prompt history. PR #2295 was tested by applying its diff onto 494f66526 rather than checking out its older branch; its full-suite numbers were not re-run here.

2319.title: provider-claude-code: unknown custom entry type agent-session-bridge-state floods sdk/unknown log
2319.rootCauseOneLine: Misattributed to provider-claude-code: Pi 0.84 emits an `entry_appended` session event for every `pi.appendEntry("agent-session-bridge-state", …)` call by the agent-session-bridge Pi extension; bb's Pi bridge forwards it as sdk/message and plugins/provider-pi/src/visibility.ts has no case for `entry_appended`, so it is classified `{kind:"sdk/unknown", coverage:"unknown"}` and persisted as a provider/unhandled row ("SDK Unknown / Raw event: sdk/unknown") on every message_end/turn_end.
2319.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-pi/src/visibility.ts add `entry_appended` to PiSdkEventType, toPiSdkEventType, the sdk/simple branch of parsePiRawEvent, and the noise group of describeParsedPiRawEvent (4-line diff saved at 2319/repro/proposed-fix-visibility.diff; verified: repro test flips, existing 57 Pi tests pass, no wire change so no protocol bump). Do the same for the other Pi 0.84 session events (session_info_changed, thinking_level_changed, queue_update, summarization_retry_*, bash_execution_update) and add a test that runs every member of the vendored SDK's AgentSessionEvent["type"] union through toPiSdkEventType so future Pi bumps fail loudly. Do not touch the Claude parser (dead code there); relabel the issue provider-claude-code -> provider-pi.
2319.caveats: The issue's quoted payload shows the custom entry directly as params.message; Pi 0.84.x actually nests it under {type:"entry_appended", entry:{...}} — both shapes hit sdk/unknown today, but the proposed fix only covers the real entry_appended shape. Live bb repro used a stand-in extension (same appendEntry calls as agent-session-bridge) injected via BB_PI_BRIDGE_COMMAND/ARGS rather than the real extension, and the anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 attempt errored on this machine's expired Pi OAuth token (the github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5 attempt succeeded; both produced the 3 unhandled rows). 'Logged heavily' could not be confirmed as bb log output: bb's server/daemon logs contain no unhandled lines; the noise is persisted provider/unhandled events (timeline rows, bb thread log, plugin event subscriptions).
